The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t),
$$

where the principal normal vector $N(t)$ is given by

$$
N(t)=\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the principal normal $N(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}\sqrt{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+{(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩}{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}})}=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the binormal vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,1⟩\times ⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t & -\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t & 1 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t & \operatorname{sin}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t & 1 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t & 1 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t & -\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t & \operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨0-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,-(0-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\sqrt{2}{sin}^{2}⁡t+\sqrt{2}{cos}^{2}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\sqrt{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
